newsitem.title: USA: Mothers Work says to restructure operations.
newsitem.headline: Mothers Work says to restructure operations.

text.p: Mothers Work Inc's said Wednesday it will restructure its core maternity business by combining the Mimi Maternity(R) and Maternite(R) over-lapping product lines and closing approximately 30 retail locations serviced by other company stores.

Mothers Work's President and Chief Operating Officer, Rebecca Matthias, said this consolidation of our maternity clothing lines is intended to improve operating performance by eliminating redundancy in product styles and store locations.

The company said it will take a charge in the second quater of $7.6 million in connection with the restructuring and related actions, the cash portion of which is about $1.3 million to be paid out through the second quarter of fiscal 1998.

The charge of $7.6 million consists of a $5.6 million charge to restructure and consolidate upscale maternity lines, a $0.8 million charge to write-down inventory related to this consolidation and $1.2 million to write-down long-lived assets at some of its continuing retail locations and for certain other costs.

In addition, the company said its loss of $7.9 million for the second quarter ended March 31, exclusive of restructuring charges of $5.6 million, was primarily attributable to its recently acquired Episode non-maternity fashion business.

Matthias said: "We are very disappointed with results of the Episode division, including its effect on the Company's performance for the quarter...the turnaround of the Episode business is taking longer than originally anticipated and management is focused on the need to improve results in that division."
Finally, the company said it has received a commitment from CoreStates Bank to extend its $20 million revolving credit facility for an additional year until July 31, 1999.
